dhp1:1: These verses describe a threefold process: intention, actions, and consequences. Each of these three “things” is included under _dhammā_. This line is phrased in prose at [an1.56]()–7; see there for further notes. | _Mano_ here is the active aspect of mind, effectively meaning _kamma_. Translating as “mind” obscures the ethical reading in favor of an idealistic one, which given the remainder of the verse is unjustified. | The MS edition on which this translation is based has headings for each of the verses. These are derived from the background stories told in the commentary. As such, I have not translated them as they are not intrinsic to the text.
dhp1:3: Intention is expressed through actions of speech and body.
dhp1:5: The consequence of bad actions is suffering. In popular culture, the consequence is often said to be _kamma_, but in early Buddhism, _kamma_ is the action that creates the consequence.
